Good catch — valid. Fixed in b374f9efe.

The Go type backing these fields is secret-aware: every credential in `objectstore.Config` is a `schemas.SecretVar`, and `SecretVar.UnmarshalJSON` accepts both a plain string (`env.X` / `vault.X` / literal) and the structured `{ value, env_var, from_env }` object. The schema already models the identical fields as a `string | object` union in `config_store.aws`, so string-only here would reject an otherwise-loadable secure config.

Changed the credential fields — `bucket`, `region`, `endpoint`, `access_key_id`, `secret_access_key`, `session_token`, `role_arn`, `credentials`, `credentials_json`, `project_id` — to `anyOf: [string, { value, env_var, from_env }]`, matching the `config_store.aws` convention. Applied to **both** `audit_logs.object_storage` and the pre-existing `logs_store.object_storage` block (which had the same gap), so the two stay consistent.

Not an issue — the consumer exists, it just lives in the enterprise repo (as expected for `audit_logs`).

`audit_logs` is enterprise-only in this public repo; per `.github/workflows/scripts/schemasync/main.go`, `/properties/audit_logs` is "defined in bifrost-enterprise/lib/config.go", so this repo only ever carries the JSON schema half. The matching runtime wiring lands in the parallel enterprise change (`feat: allow s3 storage for audit logs`):

- `lib/config.go` — adds `ObjectStorage *objectstore.Config json:"object_storage,omitempty"` to `AuditLogsConfig`, so the block is unmarshaled/consumed.
- `framework/auditlogs/archive.go` — the S3/GCS archival writer (flushes batches to `{prefix}/audit-logs/...`).
- `framework/auditlogs/buffer.go` + `server.go` — hook the archiver into the flush path.

So a schema-valid `audit_logs.object_storage` config does produce S3/GCS objects. The only real requirement — correctly implied by this comment — is release coupling: this schema PR and the enterprise consumer PR must ship in the same release, otherwise the field would validate but no-op. They're being cut together.

Acknowledged, but I'm intentionally leaving the enum as-is. The `base_provider_type` enum is not the runtime allowlist and never has been — the Go allowlist (`SupportedBaseProviders`) is only `{anthropic, bedrock, cohere, gemini, openai, huggingface, replicate}`, while this enum already contains many entries the runtime rejects as base providers: `elevenlabs`, `ollama`, `groq`, `perplexity`, `cerebras`, `deepseek`, `openrouter`, `nebius`, `xai`, `runway`, `runware`, `fireworks`, `vllm`, etc. `cartesia` was added the same way its sibling TTS provider `elevenlabs` is present.

So "schema passes, startup fails with unsupported base provider type" is a pre-existing property of ~15 enum entries, enforced consistently by `IsSupportedBaseProvider` at runtime — it is not introduced or worsened by Cartesia. Removing only `cartesia` would make it the lone TTS provider missing from the enum while `elevenlabs` stays, which is a worse inconsistency. Realigning the enum to the runtime allowlist is a legitimate cleanup, but it applies to the whole enum and belongs in its own PR, not this provider addition.

discussion_comments.comment_body:
This is intentional and follows the established convention. This Newman environment file is structurally identical to every other provider env file in `provider_config/` (e.g. `bifrost-v1-bedrock.postman_environment.json`, `bifrost-v1-anthropic.postman_environment.json`, `bifrost-v1-openai.postman_environment.json`) — none of them define `baseUrl`, `admin_username`, `openaiKey`, `vertex*`, or `vk*`/`logid*`.

Those variables belong to a different suite. The `vk*`/`logid*`/`admin_username` values are read by the **API** suite (`run-newman-api-tests.sh`), which does not consume these provider env files (it injects values via `--env-var` and its own collection). These provider env files are consumed only by the **inference** suite (`run-newman-inference-tests.sh`), which supplies shared harness values such as `provider_capabilities` separately via `-g $GLOBALS_TMP`; the env file only needs the provider-specific keys it already contains.

So no placeholders go unresolved for the inference suite, and adding those keys here would diverge from all other provider env files. Resolving as a false positive.
